body.cap: SEGYM receives CES 2025 Innovation Award in Fitness Equipment | Photo by HUMANICS

body.x: HUMANICS Co., Ltd. (CEO Jungsu Choi) announced its participation in CES 2025 in Las Vegas from January 7 to 10 at the K-Startup Pavilion.

Founded to drive the digital transformation of healthcare and rehabilitation equipment, HUMANICS aims to integrate cutting-edge human-robot fusion technologies into daily life. CEO Jungsu Choi, a gold and bronze medalist at the 2016 and 2020 Cybathlon competitions in Switzerland, leverages his expertise to develop accessible, high-tech solutions for fitness and rehabilitation.

The company's flagship product, SEGYM, launched in October 2024, is a state-of-the-art digital healthcare machine that combines motorized free-weight technology with advanced software. SEGYM recently earned a CES 2025 Innovation Award in the fitness category, marking the first time a Korean company has achieved this recognition in advanced health and exercise equipment. In Korea, SEGYM is already in use at Seoul and Gyeongbuk sports high schools for elite athlete training and at regional public fitness centers to support community fitness initiatives.

SEGYM boasts precision features such as load generation up to 300kg without manual weight changes, 0.1kg load adjustments, and real-time body balance measurement. The machine includes a robotic-assisted trainer mode, safety functions to prevent injuries from overloading, and post-exercise analysis and recommendations. These features enable users to train effectively without needing a human trainer while ensuring safety and precision.

HUMANICS plans to use CES 2025 to demonstrate SEGYM’s capabilities to international buyers, explore collaborative opportunities within the digital healthcare and fitness sectors, and gather feedback to identify new applications for its technology.

In preparation for its global expansion, HUMANICS is focusing on the European market, targeting applications in rehabilitation and welfare. Following domestic medical validation and certification processes, the company plans to showcase SEGYM at Germany’s REHACARE.

HUMANICS is expanding its offerings with new products and platforms. The upcoming Humania AI healthcare trainer platform will feature AI-powered exercise pattern analysis, personalized training suggestions, and social networking capabilities for sharing fitness information. The company is also developing a compact home-training device, SEHOME, to enhance accessibility for personal use.

A Humanics representative stated, “By integrating advanced AI and robotics, SEGYM is designed to redefine fitness and rehabilitation. Our domestic success provides a strong foundation for establishing our presence in Europe and the U.S., and we are committed to expanding our lineup to meet diverse user needs globally.”
